title: SDK Guardian: Failure Repro Lab & Quick Triage Notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact working note for the "SDK Guardian" concept: a small, reproducible lab and playbook that lets SDK engineers (and SEs) reproduce, triage, and squash customer-reported failures in under 30 minutes. The idea: curated minimal repro suites + focused telemetry slices + a short checklist to get to a root cause quickly.

Scope / what this doc is (and is not):
- IN SCOPE: SDK callflow failures (initialization, auth, request encoding, streaming fallbacks, telemetry gaps), quick repros for local dev and sandbox, triage checklist for SE handoff.
- OUT OF SCOPE: large infra incidents, serving-runtime kernel bugs, infra autoscaling behavior (link separate SRE runbook).

Goals (practical):
- Provide a 5–30 minute path from "customer report" -> "repro on dev machine or CI" -> "root-cause hypothesis".
- Reduce back-and-forth with customers by shipping a lightweight repro harness they can run.
- Standardize minimal telemetry slices we ask for in support tickets.

Quick signal checklist (first 6 items to run):
1) Confirm environment and SDK version (sdk.version, runtime). Ask customer for a single command that fails.
2) Request ID or sample request payload (truncate PII). Ask for exact headers.
3) Re-run against sandbox with --verbose and --replay-mode (local small harness).
4) Compare server-side token/timeouts from sandbox logs (if available).
5) If streaming: toggle to polling mode (helps isolate streaming framing vs model-side errors).
6) If reproducible locally, capture a short HAR / network dump + SDK debug log slice.

Minimal repro harness (dev machine):
- A tiny node/python script that:
  * loads the same SDK version as the customer
  * sets REDWOOD_ENV=sandbox and a small wrapper to inject headers
  * supports modes: single-call, streaming, batched-prefix
  * optional --payload-from-file to load large prompts
- Expectation: run in <60s. Include pre-seeded sample config files to toggle batching/quantization flags.
- Housekeeping: scripts live in /playgrounds/guardian-harness (GH#repo/sdk-guardrails).

Telemetry slices to request (make these explicit in ticket templates):
- sdk_version, os, node/python runtime version
- request headers (x-client, x-sdk-version, x-request-id)
- size of prompt + token estimate
- latency percentiles for connect / first-byte / last-byte
- error_type strings and stack traces (if generated client-side)
- server-side error codes / model id / model variant used

Triage matrix (fast hypotheses and checks):
- Hypothesis: malformed request encoding (e.g., JSON vs NDJSON) -> Check: repro with minimal JSON payload; validate Content-Type and content-length.
- Hypothesis: auth token expiry / KMS rotation -> Check: run local call with fresh token, check 401/403 logs.
- Hypothesis: streaming framing mismatch -> Check: toggle streaming->polling; check chunk boundaries in HAR.
- Hypothesis: SDK retry/backoff bug -> Check: reduce RTO to 0 and check duplicate calls; inspect retry headers.
- Hypothesis: model fallback mismatch (customer pins a model) -> Check: call explicitly with model param; compare server model selection logs.

Short reproducible examples (copy-paste snippets to include in replies):
- Node minimal single call (pseudocode):
  > node repro.js --mode=single --payload=sample.json --sdk-version=0.14.2
- Python streaming toggle:
  > python3 repro.py --mode=stream --fallback=polling --log=debug
(Include these in canned email responses to reduce friction)

Common gotchas we've seen (field notes):
- Customers forwarding SDK requests through internal proxies that strip/modify chunked encoding -> streaming breakage.
- Patchy telemetry: customer deleted debug logs, only system logs remain. Ask for earliest useful slice.
- Local environments with strict MTU or corporate proxies causing truncated frames.
- Using an outdated adapter or polyfill (fetch/nodelibs) that changes header casing.

Playbook for SE handoff (if not resolvable quickly):
- Attach minimal repro harness + instructions to reproduce in sandbox.
- Provide the telemetry slice summary in the ticket (copy from the standard template).
- Suggest 2 next steps (quick fix: toggle fallback; longer fix: SDK patch PR).
- Assign to eng-developer-experience with labels: sdk-guardian, needs-repro, severity-{low|high}.

Development tasks (short backlog):
- T1: Build guardian-harness v0.1 (node/python, single repo). Owner: Ethan. Target: 2024-11-15.
- T2: Ticket template update in Zendesk + Confluence snippet. Owner: Sofia. Target: 2024-12-01.
- T3: Add small telemetry toggle flags to SDK (opt-in) to capture chunk boundaries and raw frames. Owner: SDK team. Target: Q1 2025.
- T4: Create a short internal 15-min lab (recording + slides) for SE rotation. Owner: Ava. Target: 2025-01-10.

Open questions / decisions:
- Do we want the harness to collect (by default) raw chunk frames? Privacy concerns with raw payloads — need legal review.
- Should we require customers to run repro harness before escalation? (tradeoff: friction vs confidence).
- Where to store small customer-provided repros? S3 with TTL and access controls vs Confluence attachments.

Notes to self / snippets for replies:
- "Can you paste the exact command you ran and the full SDK log with --debug enabled? If possible, run the attached repro script and paste the single failing request id."
- "If streaming fails, can you try --fallback=polling and confirm whether the text output is produced? That tells us whether the model returned a response vs the streaming layer failing."

Artifacts / quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SDK+telemetry+schema
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-guardrails (guardian-harness folder)
- Support template: https://zendesk.redwood.ai/agent/tickets/new?template=sdk-guardian

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Draft v0 of repro harness and a short README with 3 sample commands.
- Update support ticket template with explicit telemetry checklist.
- Run 1 internal tabletop with SEs to validate the 30-minute target.

Unresolved: legal review request for raw frame capture (open with security/legal).

-- end of sketch --

(Style notes: intentionally lean, actionable steps, copy-paste friendly commands and replies. Keep this as a working canvas; we will extract a polished one-pager for public docs later.)
